Conditions signalled by zulm

Source: R/conditions.R
zulm-conditions.Rd

Every error zulm signals inherits zulm_error, and every warning zulm_warning, so a handler can catch them all or one class at a time with tryCatch() or withCallingHandlers().

Details

Errors:

  • zulm_invalid_argument: an argument of the wrong kind or value.

  • zulm_shape_error: dimensions that do not fit; carries op, the shapes and the R call where an operation is involved.

  • zulm_type_error: a tensor or value type that is not accepted.

  • zulm_unsupported_backward: an operation without a gradient on a gradient path; carries op.

  • zulm_memory_error: an allocation beyond getOption("zulm.max_bytes") (4 GiB by default); carries requested and allowed, in bytes.

  • zulm_engine_error: an assertion of the ggml library caught while a graph was being built; carries ggml_message. The graph is discarded.

  • zulm_interrupt: a computation stopped by a user interrupt; also inherits interrupt.

  • zulm_file_error: a GGUF or safetensors file that cannot be read or written.

  • zulm_arrow_error: an Arrow stream with an unsupported type, a null, a dictionary or a stream failure; carries column and row.

  • zulm_companion_error: a companion package whose interface lacks something zulm needs.

  • zulm_stale_error: an object that is no longer valid, because it was restored from a saved R session or created by a variant no longer in use.

  • zulm_internal_error: a bug in zulm.

Warnings:

  • zulm_range_warning: values beyond the range of the storage type, which became infinite.

  • zulm_nonfinite_warning: a training step whose loss is not finite.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
tryCatch(
  zl_param_get(p, "missing"),
  zulm_invalid_argument = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
#> [1] "The store has no parameter 'missing'."
